subject: fix(eve): replay sealed World streams without opening a live subscription (G-005)
source_and_call_chain_record:
Refs #2506, G-005. Base `fdbc2b95dd6cea673e3900fc2c25021f73d87134`, head `49549f7de4b3f0ac0b48a794a32bcff9a9b3ff1b`.

When a Node World reader reopens a completed stream, the bound Worker previously required a successful live WebSocket upgrade before it attempted the first durable read. The release already locks @fantasticfour/world-cloudflare 2.4.3; its StreamDO.getChunks() returns the committed bytes, closed flag and tail position together. The change reads that first page through the existing run-scoped DO, replays sealed bytes directly, and subscribes while the stream is still open. An initially empty open page is read again after subscribing so a concurrent append or close cannot be missed.

**Isolated evidence**. On Linux, workerd 1.20261019.1 with persistent DO storage, the existing Node World reader and the HTTP /world/stream consumer reproduced failure before the fix. Only the notification upgrade was disabled on the target test object after persisting 35 chunks and EOF. The base threw `Cloudflare World stream read failed`. With this tree, the same zero offset, negative offset and EOF reads all pass. Full World package: 7 files, 59 passed, 5 pre-existing upstream skips. Locked Wrangler 4.152.0 successfully bundled the release module through the existing dry-run command. No production, signing, deployment, or customer action.

**Merge risk: medium**. Alignment good, impact limited to World stream reads but shared by live and completed sessions. Verification includes replay across pages/restart, idle behavior, explicit DELETE, cancel/close races and same-name cross-run isolation. The implementation keeps the live read and cancellation protocol. Error detection uses normal stream transport failures and focused workerd regression. No state migration, reversible by ordinary revert. Current-head GitHub checks and exact merge-commit runtime receipts belong here. Existing production owner retains #1954 / mikka-cloud#155.

subject: fix(eve): use the native accepted ID for unkeyed World queue messages (G-006)
source_and_call_chain_record:
Refs #2506, G-006. Source `ebd1470f7adf39add34a5d4ccbac6457d21591d3` from `7e12e534899d586e5182f56e811e7b6ff753335d`.

Native @fantasticfour/world-cloudflare 2.4.3 mints a message ID before enqueue and returns it after its binding accepts the send. Mikka used to parse the echoed ID from a second HTTP body on every publication. For unkeyed messages the named World service has already awaited the native queue send and cannot substitute another ID. Failure of that body read made the producer report failure after execution was accepted, inviting a second submission. Keyed concurrent sends do need the DO-selected winning ID. The change selects the native receipt for unkeyed sends and consumes the authoritative body for keyed sends. Executor continuations require successful acceptance; their adapter does not consume a response ID. Pinned destinations, request authentication, delays, attempts and DLQ ownership are unchanged.

**Reproduction and evidence**. Linux, real Miniflare queues, DO-backed deduplication, and the package's real executor. Drop only the producer response body after a successful World publication. On base the handler receives the message and the producer rejects with `receipt body reset after native acceptance`. After the fix the producer resolves with the same ID observed at the executor. The full package passed 59 tests, with the 5 pre-existing upstream skips, including eight concurrent keyed producers with one winning ID, pinned redelivery/DLQ, auth failure and Stop/End control wakes. Run the existing package test via test:eve.

**Merge risk: medium**. Narrow scope but shared queue hot path. Explicit non-2xx retains transport rejection and keyed receipt loss is still a failure. Production release stays with #1954 / mikka-cloud#155. No new retries, storage, schema or platform permission; ordinary revert is sufficient. GitHub workflow and exact merge SHA evidence to follow.

subject: fix(release): keep receiptless pushes out of the promoted Desktop preflight group (G-001)
source_and_call_chain_record:
Refs #2506, G-001. Exact base `609517b3c2c3b3e4604aa52656f2b828e0d0b382`, source `c4c1d29ecc033e23834ded9b16e56cdd70547236`.

The Desktop workflow runs on main pushes and manual dispatches carrying Cloudflare serving evidence. Both entered exactly the same Actions preflight concurrency group with cancel-in-progress enabled. A normal push can therefore cancel a release owner's in-flight verification and then fail the legacy provider guard itself. [Actual receiptless main push failure](https://github.com/alexj11324/Mikka/actions/runs/43601159627/job/132465991899). This is a separate scheduler issue from F's ARCH2-013, which supplies the correct observation verifier; its proof checks stay intact.

The existing GitHub scheduler now supersedes only waits in the same release path and ref. The paid macOS signer still uses one shared concurrency group, and source, overlay, promotion, live-serving, signing and rollback checks keep their existing owners.

**Reproduction.** Evaluated the actual workflow YAML with GitHub's @actions/expressions 0.3.34 on Linux. On base, main push (no inputs) and main manual dispatch (`actions:101:1`) both resolve to `desktop-release-preflight`; the distinct-group assertion fails. In the fix they resolve to `desktop-release-preflight-refs/heads/main-legacy` and `desktop-release-preflight-refs/heads/main-promoted`. Explicit receiptless/manual and push still coalesce; different promoted receipts on main still coalesce; a different ref is isolated; both modes retain the same non-cancelling macOS group. The project regression pins this behavior. All 61 release, promotion and overlay checks passed, zero skips. No live release was dispatched; no production cancellation is asserted.

**Merge risk: low.** Narrow job-scheduler input only. It neither enables a release nor treats failed evidence as success. Revert the concurrency group to undo; release qualification and visibility stay on the existing jobs. Official [concurrency semantics](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency).

subject: fix(task-sandbox): retire native writers before the one archive sweep (G-010)
source_and_call_chain_record:
G-010 / #2506. Task file and recovery path: TaskMachines.park → the per-task Durable Object → native writer quiesce → SDK DirectoryBackup + manifest → container destruction and quota release → existing archive maintenance. @cloudflare/sandbox 1.0.3. The common native-writer checkpoint helper was sweeping R2 and the stop procedure swept the same task prefix a second time. An R2 listing failure in the first sweep could prevent container destruction and release of a slot even though the recoverable checkpoint already existed.

Source 152348d0da9fc9fb73618e3ec1e867c5837a6dff, base 4e0c8bc83d39e0f1794c5cb1fa8472ba3b3784fd. Reproduced on the original exported TaskMachine.park with a scoped grant, native writer, actual stop() and substituted storage/container/backup ports: first sweep saw state ‘stopping’ rather than ‘stopped’, preventing retirement. After change ordering is quiesce, backup, destroy, release, sweep; the same saved checkpoint is returned. Move cleanup to each existing owner. Normal process completion still prunes after checkpoint; a stopped machine uses its existing sweep and alarm. Same archive exclusions, rollback manifest, scoped prefix, signed grant and quota fence. No new controller or timer. Linux source tests 10/10, node --test cloudflare/task-sandbox/*.test.mjs. Hardware/provider acceptance remains with the existing release owner. #1874 concerns a different provider and its PR has no changes in the task sandbox.

subject: Let bundled chat send through main when the renderer is offline
source_and_call_chain_record:
G-012，关联 #2506。基线 `702b6e1bf1bc720675f63db286c05a1d20f401f8`，源 `1d9ec7f9b475cf701f190efe2216ecab7f3deba1`。

个人/Bot composer、群聊 composer、任务线程和 Inbox 共用的回复命令会在 `navigator.onLine === false` 时直接显示“未发送”。普通 Web 的离线草稿与显式重试有实际产品合同。打包桌面的请求从隔离 preload 确认的本地 renderer，经 `mikka://app` 的路由许可及 `BundledAuth.request`，最后由主进程独立的 Electron session.fetch 发出。渲染进程的网络状况不能替主进程作这一判定。

在 Linux 锁版 Electron 45.1.0，加载本地页面后，从页面 POST 群聊地址，经本仓实际自定义协议、鉴权对象、独立 Electron 后端分区，送至只接收隔离测试身份的 loopback HTTP 服务。正常时观测 `[true, 202]`；仅更改 renderer 网络状态或对其执行完整 CDP 断网时，均观测 `[false, 202]`，每个动作各收到一次带正确身份的请求。基线已挂载个人 composer 的 bundled 场景实际提交 0 次，预期 1 次；普通 Web 的失败气泡和重试对照通过。

三处已有发送入口共用一次判断，打包桌面直接走其既有传输。版本、业务授权、实际请求错误、拒绝反馈、命令 ID、Web 离线行为保留。针对个人、群聊、线程/Inbox 三套已挂载入口的测试 102/102 通过；正式 CI 与精确合后验收回填本单。无正式发布或真机签名。

subject: fix: report Linear recovery through the native Cloudflare Cron invocation (G-014)
source_and_call_chain_record:
Refs #2506, G-014. The 04:00 UTC trigger added in 83874b62cdeeedddfc1b45963850d4b9eada5fe3 silently skipped enabled Linear recovery if the independent manual HTTP endpoint had no bearer secret. It also caught batch exceptions and resolved the promise supplied to Cloudflare, turning a failed delivery into a successful native Cron invocation.

## Cloudflare contract and impact

[Scheduled handler](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/handlers/scheduled/) and [Cron Triggers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/cron-triggers/) define the invocation and its promise lifetime. `cloudflare/linear-sync/wrangler.jsonc` selects `0 4 * * *`, compatibility date 2026-10-22, and Wrangler 4.152.0 is pinned. The handler now owns its single promise, calls the existing gated sync batch in a request-scoped Hyperdrive connection and reports failed execution. Removed the transport-specific credential check from native execution, the detached wrapper/sole helper and the handler that converted failure to fulfillment. The HTTP route still returns 503 on an unset bearer and 401 for an incorrect bearer. The business switch, OAuth binding requirements, inbox and outbox claim rules, webhook signature validation, cleanup and manual HTTP contract retain their original owners. The only new serialization uses the existing cause-fields implementation to keep database/provider error text out of native exception logs.

## Verification

- Base `b19eed9081d9858686d57547e7afcec73d6e9005` failed the new native invocation regression with “Missing expected rejection”. The fixture exercised the original returned or registered promises.
- Candidate `cec72ce903bb6e05dce9450a1975bfe17b31e2bf`, cloud Linux, workspace lock-matched dependencies: complete `test:linear-sync` package script passed 53 + 7 tests, zero skips. Focused oxlint and repository UI policy passed.
- Wrangler 4.152.0 bundled the actual Worker offline. Invoking its actual scheduled entry with the enabled test flag and missing sync configuration on isolated workerd 1.20261019.1 returned `{outcome:"exception",noRetry:false}`; the separate manual HTTP request returned 503. The local binary supports an older compatibility date than the production configuration, so this remains an isolated result.
- PostgreSQL 17.11, clean throw-away cluster, repository E2E migrations, a synthetic inbox row and local flag/provider boundary. The actual handler, DB scope and batch processed two concurrent native invocations and a later replay without an HTTP bearer. SQL readback was `done, attempts=1`. Removing the fixture inbox table produced a rejected invocation with sanitized Postgres cause `42P01`. No live provider or production writes.
- Scope is one Worker plus its tests and existing operator page. Risk is limited to surfacing failed enabled sweeps or executing them when manual HTTP is unconfigured. Normal revert restores prior behavior without a schema migration. Affected validation is observable through Cron status and protected CI. Production acceptance stays with #1954 and private release owner #155.

subject: Use native Durable Object name lookup for World streams (G-018)
source_and_call_chain_record:
Refs #2506, G-018. Baseline `b19eed9081d9858686d57547e7afcec73d6e9005`. Source `368f16c6753bc0200d089d5f424dac4f87c96730`.

The business World previously fabricated a two-method Durable Object namespace to prepend its persisted workload name. Each lookup forwarded through `get(idFromName(name))`. Both the registry and individual stream now call the native `getByName` API directly. The naming policy retains identical bytes for both workloads. Stream-only RPCs also dispense with an unrelated workflow authority stub. Host, workload and namespace checks remain at the private entrypoint.

[Cloudflare Durable Object namespace API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/namespace/#getbyname) · Wrangler 4.152.0, Miniflare 5.20261019.2-beta, workerd 1.20261019.1, project compatibility date 2026-10-22. World 5.1.0, upstream Cloudflare World 2.4.3. Original scoped transport introduced in `372db8b93f9e778993f4be3c5a9236a8ab08f164`.

Node World → private Eve/business binding → stream RPC or raw stream GET/DELETE → named run registry or stream DO. Normal registration/append/close/EOF, subscriber cancellation, shared-storage business isolation and direct stream service now use the same primitive. The regression seeds existing objects through their old keys, including the business key’s nested serialization. Both clients list and append to those same objects; the previous lookup reads back the two bytes.

Cloud Linux isolated native workerd and SQLite, complete World package: 7 files, 61 passed, 5 pre-existing upstream skips. All three JS files pass Node syntax checks; `git diff --check` passed. Production deployment remains with #1954.

**Merge risk: medium.** Alignment good. Impact is scoped to durable stream identity and private routing. Verification uses both workload bindings, real persisted objects and previous serialized keys. Rollback is an ordinary revert with zero migration. Missing registry entries or unread prior bytes fail the added compatibility regression; the runtime transport retains its existing error handling.

subject: perf: let Cloudflare schedule maintenance only on due quarter hours (G-017)
source_and_call_chain_record:
Refs #2506, G-017. Baseline b19eed9081d9858686d57547e7afcec73d6e9005. The Worker currently wakes 60 times an hour for 4 useful ticks. The 56 idle native invocations cost runtime resources while making zero business HTTP calls. Commit a7142430b7db88e1f4a0810eb1b63244c37a3695 consolidated several schedules to one because of the account-level trigger ceiling. The single-trigger requirement remains satisfied.

## Native contract and removal
The [Cloudflare Cron Trigger documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/cron-triggers/) lists comma-separated minute values, exact event expressions and propagation up to 15 minutes. [Worker limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/) are per account. The reviewed Wrangler configuration selects one `0,15,30,45 * * * *` trigger, compatibility date 2026-10-22, pinned Wrangler 4.152.0. We use the minute list so callers of the older *individual* `*/15` briefing expression keep that documented single-endpoint contract.
- Cloudflare's event owns the cadence. Removed generic sweep interval configuration, filter and repetitive due checks. The remaining dispatcher selects 3 quarter-hour handlers, 2 extra hourly operations or 1 half-hour operation using the event time. Cloudflare owns the promise and its failure outcome. The previous minute expression accepts only events still propagating, with zero traffic off-quarter. Its gate is required for already registered events; no fallback timer is installed in the hosted Worker.
- Shared self-hosted and local development consumers call the same business dispatcher. Offline leadership and local clock handling remain on installations without Cloudflare. The dev clock now sleeps to the next UTC quarter. The Worker entry exports only its actual handler. The publisher hashes both executable modules and tests preserve independent endpoint acceptance, auth, failures and safe numeric logs.
- Public release selection and existing protected publisher stay in place. The preflight accepts exactly the existing minute or desired quarter-hour setting with expected bindings and exposures. Only the desired cadence passes readback after the single Wrangler write. An inconclusive upload is still not repeated.

## Acceptance
At the old SHA the new Wrangler contract regression failed (minute literal versus quarter hour). Source ffdd7d24491ccfd8170ddc98d3184ccaa218b202 passed all 41 Worker, publisher, local-service and 2 built-in scheduler tests, no skips, and affected oxlint. A period-by-period comparison over one hour contains identical authorized business requests. The Wrangler-built module was dispatched through isolated workerd 1.20261019.1 using all four occurrence times computed from the exact configuration. The six independent endpoint counts were 4, 4, 4, 1, 1 and 1. One upstream 503 yielded a native exception after all three quarter-hour calls. The local runtime predates the production compatibility date.

Risk and ownership: one reversible Worker schedule and its matching source. A later production promotion must verify exact remote trigger and observe the three UTC boundary cases; watcher and receipt ownership remain with #1954 and the existing private edge publisher. This PR makes no production writes. Reverting a deployed change requires restoring the old trigger through the existing protected publisher and confirming its active source and settings; platform propagation may overlap, and downstream writes retain their existing idempotency.

subject: G-030 · Use the native R2 PUT result for the retained Eve archive
source_and_call_chain_record:

Immutable key, remembered cleanup, deadline, capacity and operator-approved build scope remain enforced. Native local workerd/Miniflare R2 with the actual retention function and FixedLengthStream: baseline recorded PUT then HEAD. On this source, the same 21-byte synthetic artifact yields one PUT; the independent GET matches the original bytes, length, digest, and release. subject: G-033 · Reclaim a finished first task backup after its checkpoint commit is interrupted
source_and_call_chain_record:
Refs #2506. Source `3a1fc7765b5b79df17127258222792218629706f`, base `e0b64498c7396adbfd15e504ff9898f68d9c2186`. The [original workspace persistence implementation](https://github.com/alexj11324/Mikka/commit/514fcd20d1464dd62a2314765c0cfba85f80865e) uses @cloudflare/sandbox 1.0.3 [DirectoryBackup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/reference/directory-backups/) and a per-task Durable Object manifest. G-010 [#2517](https://github.com/alexj11324/Mikka/pull/2517) already retired compute before archive cleanup. This is a separate first-write case in that cleanup.

Native backup can successfully complete its immutable R2 object immediately before storage.put('checkpoint') is lost. The product restores only from its committed manifest. The old prune returned as soon as there was no manifest, so a stopped-task alarm or terminal cleanup could never remove the completed first orphan. The same existing sweep now treats the retained set as empty in that state. When a manifest exists, the previously committed object remains protected. The listed prefix, UUID/suffix checks, paginated traversal, existing batch [R2 delete](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/workers/workers-api-reference/), task DO serialization, and recovery fence all stay in force. Native aborted multipart cleanup is independently scoped to incomplete uploads; an account read of workspace bucket lifecycle found no rule deleting already-completed task archives. The product does not scan unrelated buckets or delete from production as part of acceptance.

Isolated fixed-source run of the real TaskMachine.alarm → TaskWorkspace.prune against scoped storage/R2 ports reproduced the leaking UUID archive on the parent and removed only that archive on the change. New regression drives the real checkpoint method with a successful SDK-port upload followed by interrupted manifest persistence, checks restore unavailable before commit, verifies cleanup, then keeps the committed object, a neighboring task, and a nonarchive key across two replays. Protected Linux checks own the repository suite and the exact main run owns post-merge verification. No customer object was accessed.

subject: fix(mobile): finish installation discovery before probing legacy versions (G-035)

**Affected entry.** Native sign-in → ServerSelection.check → probeMobileServer → unauthenticated /api/desktop/discovery. For a bare origin, the old implementation inserted /api/version between root discovery and /mikka discovery. A slow root legacy reply could spend the shared deadline and misclassify a working installation. Check the existing modern candidates first, then ask only candidates that actually returned an HTTP response for their legacy marker. Stop once that marker identifies an old installation. The explicit installation path, compatibility/upgrade decisions, caller cancellation, one shared deadline, omitted credentials and disallowed redirects use the existing contracts. No account is selected or saved by the probe.

**Regression and acceptance.** The existing mobile discovery test now asserts the complete two-request order for a working /mikka. Added focused cases for a failed root transport and the old legacy response consuming the remaining deadline. Included in the normal `pnpm test:mobile` target. Source inspection and the regression files are available; the protected Linux test and exact merge acceptance will be recorded separately. No signed device or deployed mobile result claimed.

**Merge risk.** Change is confined to when optional legacy identification runs in a user-initiated mobile probe. Old server identification is covered by the existing fixture plus a new affected-path case; root-only and typed installation contracts stay intact. Rollback is one normal revert of the two mobile files; there is no storage, permission, signing, or schema change. Mobile OTA acceptance remains tied to the eventual exact merge and the existing owner gates.

subject: G-036 · Compare cron bearer digests with the native timing-safe primitive
source_and_call_chain_record:
Refs #2506. Source d34dd5b120a221c5441cd3e8408a5606b4ec9359 from 081556f62683312c4924434b04adec4a245375fe. This removes the JavaScript byte-by-byte XOR and both temporary views from the shared bearer verifier. Directly compare the two existing 32-byte SHA-256 HMAC outputs using the native constant-time primitive. No new credential, request protocol, configuration or fallback.

#903 unified 13 cron HTTP guards, the manual Linear Worker route and delegated enterprise cron authority. They require exactly the existing Bearer format, no-store 503 for absent configuration, no-store 401 for invalid credentials, and no comparison of raw inputs at different lengths. The same two HMACs are still computed in parallel. No claim of fewer cryptographic operations. The deployed Linear Worker uses compatibility date 2026-10-22 and nodejs_compat; the Node server and CI use 24.x. Cloudflare supports node:crypto including timingSafeEqual. Node accepts the Web Crypto ArrayBuffer results directly.

Contracts: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/nodejs/crypto/ and https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/crypto.html#cryptotimingsafeequala-b . Existing pnpm test:linear-sync includes the actual bearer and Worker fetch functions, exact, empty, malformed, shorter and longer values, plus the guard HTTP status/cache contract. Existing scoped-authority checks stay in the normal repository suites. Protected checks and exact merged runtime evidence will be recorded in #2506.

subject: G-038 · Retry due-timer handover only from the environment’s latest deployment
source_and_call_chain_record:
Refs #2506. Base 081556f62683312c4924434b04adec4a245375fe, source 13742a279767404812f0adcb4547a286568dff84. #1410 / #1411 introduced the per-process, per-kind cache and latest handover. The #1419 review recorded both missed cases. #1423 subsequently shipped the original #1411 head. The current public implementation still marked a kind current before attempting cancel, and treated every different deployment as older. The Cloudflare quarter-hour /api/cron/reconcile and write-triggered arm share this function.

Use the Workflow 5.2.3 World’s environment-scoped latest deployment before cancelling a mismatched holder. Only cache a durably observed holder on the caller’s deployment. A failed cancel or failed successor start leaves the kind eligible for the next arm. New timers started on a Vercel deployment use the SDK's latest target, including after a concurrent promotion. Local starts without deployment identity still use the current world; worlds without a latest resolver cannot authorize cancelling a different deployment. The native hook selects the business runner across races. Production run-recovery remains delegated to #1403, and ordinary GET response/tenant scope are preserved.

Executed old/new real replacement function bodies with a controlled Workflow boundary. First cancellation error + second reconcile: old code performed one cancel and never retired the old holder; new code retried the same holder and started the current deployment once. Old caller with newer holder: old code cancelled the new run and started one on the older caller; new code made zero cancel/start calls. Unavailable latest resolver made zero mutations; production recovery made zero SDK calls in the generic replacer. Added both multi-arm regressions to existing pnpm test:schedules. The source and exact postmerge Ubuntu CI will be recorded under #2506. No production mutations or credentials used.
